task.title: Atomic staged resource ownership
task.specification: Config resources is a list of unique resource IDs. Events begin{id,resources}, prepare{id}, commit{id}, abort{id}; begin resource list is nonempty unique and drawn from config. Jobs are never reused once begun. Begin succeeds only for unseen id and all requested resources free, status=begun; otherwise blocked. Prepare changes active->prepared (prepared); any other phase=invalid. Commit only prepared jobs, releases all resources, records done (committed); otherwise invalid. Abort only active/prepared jobs, releases resources, records aborted (aborted); otherwise invalid. Output {status,held:{owned_resource:job_id},done:[sorted committed IDs]}. A blocked begin does not consume the ID; an aborted ID remains used. Implement pure solve({config,state,event})->{state,output}; initial state is null. Only the current event is available; each named event uses a type field, e.g. {type:"run"}. Inputs have at most eight single lowercase ASCII-letter identifiers, safe integer quantities and at most 48 events. Return exactly the documented output fields after every event; state representation is unrestricted JSON. All identifiers and numeric fields shown in event forms are present; quantities and all intermediate arithmetic are safe integers. Integral JSON number spellings such as 1 and 1.0 are equivalent; booleans remain distinct from numbers. Regimes vary event order and timing: ordinary uses moderate capacity, boundary tests equality/empty cases, adversarial repeats stale/conflicting events, and shift uses smaller capacities or larger costs/delays within the same semantics. Generator regimes: Shift reduces the resource universe from three to two, increasing shared-resource contention. Adversarial traces add adjacent repeated events, capped at 48; those events obey the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Archival provenance and original order
matchedCard.relation: The origin and original arrangement of records preserve relationships that can be lost when the same contents are rearranged arbitrarily. A later description or arrangement is distinct from evidence of the organization in which the records were produced.
assumptions: The origin or original order is known or supported by evidence.
Relationships among records contribute to their interpretation.
matchedCard.boundary: Original order can be lost or disrupted. A newly devised arrangement does not establish that it was the historical arrangement, and provenance does not make every recorded claim true.
matchedCard.source_fact: The National Archives explains provenance, preserving or restoring original order, and devising arrangements when necessary, emphasizing the evidential significance of context.

shuffledCard.label: Seed banking
shuffledCard.relation: Preserving a reserve and preserving its ability to reactivate are different conditions. Suitable material remains in controlled storage, while periodic sample recovery provides evidence of continued viability. Duplicate holdings reduce dependence on one location.
assumptions: The material tolerates the chosen storage treatment.
Samples provide relevant evidence about the collection they represent.
Duplicate collections remain identifiable as corresponding holdings.
shuffledCard.boundary: Some material cannot survive drying or freezing. Successful retention alone does not demonstrate viability, and sampled viability is not certainty about every stored item.
shuffledCard.source_fact: Kew stores suitable dried seeds in cold vaults, periodically tests germination, and commonly duplicates holdings in their country of origin. Some seeds do not tolerate conventional storage.

sources.title: How to preserve seeds for the future

initial.explanation: Rule: after each event, output is the exact observable projection of the updated resource/job ledger. Begin is atomic: it succeeds only when the ID is unused and every requested resource is free; otherwise it is blocked without consuming the ID. Prepare, commit, and abort enforce their phase transitions. A counterexample changing held[x] violates this projection invariant.
initial.mapping: Map resources to current owners, IDs to phases, and committed IDs to done. The event determines a status and ledger transition; output projects held, sorted done IDs, and that status.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated identifier, resource, event, and numeric constraints. JSON object key order is not semantically significant.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!applies(input)||!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;var j={},h={},d=[],u={},R=input.config.resources;function eq(a,b){return JSON.stringify(a)===JSON.stringify(b)}function view(s){var q={status:s,held:{},done:d.slice().sort()};for(var i=0;i<R.length;i++)if(h[R[i]]!==undefined)q.held[R[i]]=h[R[i]];return q}for(var k=0;k<input.events.length;k++){var e=input.events[k],st='invalid',id=e.id;if(e.type==='begin'){var ok=!u[id];if(ok)for(var i=0;i<e.resources.length;i++)if(h[e.resources[i]]!==undefined)ok=false;if(ok){u[id]=1;j[id]={p:'active',r:e.resources.slice()};for(i=0;i<e.resources.length;i++)h[e.resources[i]]=id;st='begun'}else st='blocked'}else if(e.type==='prepare'&&j[id]&&j[id].p==='active'){j[id].p='prepared';st='prepared'}else if(e.type==='commit'&&j[id]&&j[id].p==='prepared'){for(var z of j[id].r)delete h[z];d.push(id);j[id].p='committed';st='committed'}else if(e.type==='abort'&&j[id]&&(j[id].p==='active'||j[id].p==='prepared')){for(var z of j[id].r)delete h[z];j[id].p='aborted';st='aborted'}if(!eq(output[k],view(st)))return false}return true}

final.explanation: Maintains job phases, resource ownership, consumed identifiers, and committed IDs. Begin is atomic and does not consume an identifier when blocked. Prepare, commit, and abort apply only to permitted phases; terminal jobs remain recorded. Each output reports the event status, current held resources, and sorted committed IDs.

initial.explanation: Maintain job phases and resource ownership. A begin is atomic: it succeeds only when the identifier is unused and every requested resource is free. Prepare, commit, and abort enforce their phase rules; releasing resources is atomic with terminal transitions.
initial.mapping: jobs maps IDs to phase and requested resources; held maps resources to active or prepared job IDs; done stores committed IDs.
initial.assumptions: Event fields are valid as specified. Output object key ordering is not semantically significant; done is sorted lexicographically.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){let s=null;for(let e of input.events){let r=solve({config:input.config,state:s,event:e});s=r.state;let o=r.output;if(!o||typeof o.status!=="string"||!o.held||!Array.isArray(o.done))return false;let d=o.done.slice().sort();if(JSON.stringify(d)!==JSON.stringify(o.done))return false;for(let k in o.held)if(!input.config.resources.includes(k))return false}return true}
initial.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let s=state||{j:{},h:{},d:[]},e=event,id=e.id,status="invalid";if(e.type==="begin"){let ok=!s.j[id]&&e.resources.every(r=>s.h[r]===undefined);if(ok){s.j[id]={p:"active",r:e.resources.slice()};for(let r of e.resources)s.h[r]=id;status="begun"}else status="blocked"}else{let j=s.j[id];if(e.type==="prepare"){if(j&&j.p==="active"){j.p="prepared";status="prepared"}}else if(e.type==="commit"){if(j&&j.p==="prepared"){for(let r of j.r)delete s.h[r];j.p="committed";s.d.push(id);status="committed"}}else if(e.type==="abort"){if(j&&(j.p==="active"||j.p==="prepared")){for(let r of j.r)delete s.h[r];j.p="aborted";status="aborted"}}}let held={};for(let r of config.resources)if(s.h[r]!==undefined)held[r]=s.h[r];return{state:s,output:{status:status,held:held,done:s.d.slice().sort()}}}

final.explanation: A begin is atomic and succeeds only when its job ID has never been begun and every requested resource is free. Successful jobs retain their requested resources through active and prepared phases. Prepare is valid only for active jobs. Commit is valid only for prepared jobs, records the ID as done, and releases resources. Abort is valid only for active or prepared jobs, marks the job aborted, and releases resources. Blocked begins leave all state unchanged and do not consume the ID; terminal jobs remain recorded so their IDs cannot be reused.
final.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let s=state||{jobs:{},held:{},done:[]},e=event,id=e.id,status="invalid",j=s.jobs[id];if(e.type==="begin"){let ok=!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.jobs,id);if(ok)for(let r of e.resources)if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.held,r)){ok=false;break}if(ok){s.jobs[id]={phase:"active",resources:e.resources.slice()};for(let r of e.resources)s.held[r]=id;status="begun"}else status="blocked"}else if(e.type==="prepare"){if(j&&j.phase==="active"){j.phase="prepared";status="prepared"}}else if(e.type==="commit"){if(j&&j.phase==="prepared"){for(let r of j.resources)delete s.held[r];j.phase="committed";s.done.push(id);status="committed"}}else if(e.type==="abort"){if(j&&(j.phase==="active"||j.phase==="prepared")){for(let r of j.resources)delete s.held[r];j.phase="aborted";status="aborted"}}let held={};for(let r of config.resources)if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.held,r))held[r]=s.held[r];return{state:s,output:{status:status,held:held,done:s.done.slice().sort()}}}

initial.explanation: Maintain each begun job’s phase and resources, plus current ownership and committed IDs. A begin is atomic: it succeeds only when the ID is unused and every requested resource is free. Prepare, commit, and abort enforce the stated phase transitions.
initial.mapping: The state maps job IDs to phases and resource lists, held maps resources to owners, and done stores committed IDs. The output status reports the current event result; held and sorted done expose the resulting aggregate state.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the documented identifier, resource, event, and numeric constraints. Resource and job identifiers are strings, and event types are exactly begin, prepare, commit, or abort.
initial.holds: function holds(input,out){if(!Array.isArray(out)||!input||!input.config)return false;let s=null;for(let i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){let r=solve({config:input.config,state:s,event:input.events[i]});s=r.state;let a=out[i],b=r.output;if(!a||a.status!==b.status||JSON.stringify(a.held)!==JSON.stringify(b.held)||JSON.stringify(a.done)!==JSON.stringify(b.done))return false}return out.length===input.events.length}
initial.program: function solve(x){let c=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state;if(!s)s={j:{},h:{},d:[]};else{s={j:Object.assign({},s.j),h:Object.assign({},s.h),d:s.d.slice()};for(let k in s.j)s.j[k]=Object.assign({},s.j[k],{r:s.j[k].r.slice()})}let status="invalid",id=e.id;if(e.type==="begin"){let ok=!s.j[id];if(ok)for(let i=0;i<e.resources.length;i++)if(s.h[e.resources[i]]!==undefined)ok=false;if(ok){s.j[id]={p:"active",r:e.resources.slice()};for(let i=0;i<e.resources.length;i++)s.h[e.resources[i]]=id;status="begun"}else status="blocked"}else if(s.j[id]){let j=s.j[id];if(e.type==="prepare"){if(j.p==="active"){j.p="prepared";status="prepared"}}else if(e.type==="commit"){if(j.p==="prepared"){j.p="committed";for(let i=0;i<j.r.length;i++)delete s.h[j.r[i]];s.d.push(id);s.d.sort();status="committed"}}else if(e.type==="abort"){if(j.p==="active"||j.p==="prepared"){j.p="aborted";for(let i=0;i<j.r.length;i++)delete s.h[j.r[i]];status="aborted"}}}let held={};for(let i=0;i<c.resources.length;i++){let k=c.resources[i];if(s.h[k]!==undefined)held[k]=s.h[k]}return{state:s,output:{status:status,held:held,done:s.d.slice()}}}

final.explanation: Track each begun job, its phase, and its owned resources. A begin is atomic and does not consume an ID when blocked. Prepare, commit, and abort enforce the required phase transitions; terminal jobs remain recorded so IDs cannot be reused. Ownership is released on commit or abort, and output exposes only configured held resources plus sorted committed IDs.
final.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state;if(s==null)s={j:{},h:{},d:[]};else{var j0=s.j||{},h0=s.h||{},d0=s.d||[];s={j:{},h:Object.assign({},h0),d:d0.slice()};for(var q in j0){s.j[q]={p:j0[q].p,r:(j0[q].r||[]).slice()}}}var id=e.id,st="invalid",j;if(e.type==="begin"){var ok=!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.j,id);if(ok)for(var i=0;i<e.resources.length;i++)if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.h,e.resources[i])){ok=false;break}if(ok){s.j[id]={p:"active",r:e.resources.slice()};for(i=0;i<e.resources.length;i++)s.h[e.resources[i]]=id;st="begun"}else st="blocked"}else if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.j,id)){j=s.j[id];if(e.type==="prepare"&&j.p==="active"){j.p="prepared";st="prepared"}else if(e.type==="commit"&&j.p==="prepared"){j.p="committed";for(var k=0;k<j.r.length;k++)delete s.h[j.r[k]];s.d.push(id);s.d.sort();st="committed"}else if(e.type==="abort"&&(j.p==="active"||j.p==="prepared")){j.p="aborted";for(var z=0;z<j.r.length;z++)delete s.h[j.r[z]];st="aborted"}}var held={};for(var a=0;a<c.resources.length;a++){var r=c.resources[a];if(Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(s.h,r))held[r]=s.h[r]}return{state:s,output:{status:st,held:held,done:s.d.slice()}}}
